items.stem: Write a class CircularQueue of fixed capacity using a list and front/rear indices that wrap with modulo arithmetic. Provide enqueue(x) (returns False when full), dequeue() (returns None when empty) and is_full().
items.markingKey:
Model answer (Python; an equivalent Java solution is equally acceptable):
class CircularQueue:
    def __init__(self, capacity):
        self.data = [None] * capacity
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.front = 0
        self.count = 0

    def is_full(self):
        return self.count == self.capacity

    def enqueue(self, x):
        if self.is_full():
            return False
        rear = (self.front + self.count) % self.capacity
        self.data[rear] = x
        self.count += 1
        return True

    def dequeue(self):
        if self.count == 0:
            return None
        x = self.data[self.front]
        self.front = (self.front + 1) % self.capacity
        self.count -= 1
        return x
Marks: correct class/method headers and parameters; correct use of attributes (self/this); correct logic and validation; correct return values/output. Tested with:
q = CircularQueue(3)
assert q.enqueue(1) and q.enqueue(2) and q.enqueue(3) and not q.enqueue(4)
assert q.dequeue() == 1 and q.enqueue(4)
assert [q.dequeue(), q.dequeue(), q.dequeue(), q.dequeue()] == [2, 3, 4, None]
